chunks.arabic_text: رَوَى ٱلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ رِجَالِهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ:

translations.en: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from some of his men, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: فِي رَجُلٍ رَكَلَ ٱمْرَأَةً فِي فَرْجِهَا فَزَعَمَتْ أَنَّهَا لَا تَحِيضُ وَكَانَ طَمْثُهَا مُسْتَقِيمًا

translations.en: Concerning a man who kicked a woman in her private part, and she claimed that she no longer menstruated, while her menstruation had previously been regular.

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ «يُتَرَبَّصُ بِهَا سَنَةً فَإِنْ رَجَعَ إِلَيْهَا ٱلطَّمْثُ وَإِلَّا غُرِّمَ ٱلرَّجُلُ ثُلُثَ دِيَتِهَا لِفَسَادِ طَمْثِهَا وَعَقْرِ رَحِمِهَا».

translations.en: He عليه السلام said: "She should be waited on for one year. If menstruation returns to her, otherwise the man is made liable for one-third of her blood money for the corruption of her menstruation and the injury to her womb."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding bodily injury inflicted upon a woman that disrupts her regular menstruation. The Imam عليه السلام orders a waiting period of one year to verify whether the condition is lasting, and if it does not return, the offender must pay one-third of her diyyah for the damage caused.
en.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman’s menstruation stops after a man injures her private area?

key_terms.ثُلُثَ دِيَتِهَا: one-third of her blood money compensation
key_terms.عَقْرِ رَحِمِهَا: injury to her womb leading to impairment
